title: The Diamond Is Not Yours
hook: A diamond sits on the left. The sign says two.
scene: Fog at dusk on 167, a diamond on the pavement and a sign that does not need words if you already know the paint. HOV. Two or more, or a motorcycle, or a bus that earned it. The Ledger is one tired man and a cat. The left looks empty and fast. Solid white fences it. The schedule wants the empty. The paint wants a number you do not have.
decision: The diamond lane is empty and fenced with solid white. Do you take it?

options.text: Take it — a bus is basically transit and the lane is wasted empty
options.result: You cross the solid. You are not a carpool and you are not the coach that earned it. A remnant in a cap is in the next ramp. The diamond was not a suggestion.

options.text: Leave it. Stay in the general lane. Solid white is the fence.
options.result: You stay out. The empty stays empty. The general lane is slower and legal. The schedule takes the minutes. The paint keeps its number.

options.text: Take it only to the next ramp, then drop back before anyone cares
options.result: A short theft is still a theft of a restricted lane. You crossed the solid. The remnant in the cap does not grade on duration.

options.text: Use it only to pass, then come back before the next ramp
options.result: Carpool lanes are not passing lanes. You still crossed the solid. The empty was not a gift.

debrief: HOV paint and a diamond mark a lane you enter only if you meet the posted occupancy. Solid white is the fence. A bus with one driver is still one.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Do not enter an HOV lane unless you meet the occupancy; solid white separates it from general lanes.
